result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.weakly_connected_components()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Get all weakly connected components as sets of node IDs. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L42842-L42896){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.weakly_connected_components() ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Weakly connected components](/assets/graphs/weakly-connected-components.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="A directed graph: a cycle A to B to C to A, a one-way edge C to D, a two-way pair D and E, and a separate edge F to G. Ignoring arrow direction leaves two pieces, A to E in the accent color and F, G in teal, which the card lists as the two weak components." width="100%"} For undirected graphs, returns regular connected components. For directed graphs, treats all edges as undirected (ignoring direction) when finding components. A weakly connected component is a maximal set of nodes where every node is reachable from every other node when edge directions are ignored. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [list[set[int]]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : List of sets, where each set contains the node IDs in a component. Components are returned in no particular order. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Ignoring edge direction, this graph has two disconnected pairs of nodes, so it returns two node sets: ::: {#32e189a3 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph(directed=True) .add_nodes(["A", "B", "X", "Y"]) .add_edges([("A", "B"), ("X", "Y")]) ) components = graph.weakly_connected_components() # Returns 2 len(components) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 2 ``` ::: ::: Adding an isolated node to a connected chain creates a second, single-node component, which is easy to spot by finding the largest component with `max`: ::: {#a04103bb .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ec.Graph(directed=False) graph.add_path_graph(10) # Connected chain of 10 nodes graph.add_node(label="isolated") components = graph.weakly_connected_components() largest = max(components, key=len) # Returns 10 (the connected chain, excluding the isolated node) len(largest) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` 10 ``` ::: :::
